correctness.rationale: The edge identity B=DM^{-1}D^T is positive-definite tridiagonal with nonpositive off-diagonals; positive principal minors and tridiagonal elimination establish (I+BA)^-1>=0 for every diagonal A>=0. Condition w^TB>=0 makes its weighted column sums <=w. Convex divided differences reduce arbitrary smooth proximal comparisons to this inverse, and smooth approximation handles nonsmooth finite convex energies. Nonlinear flows follow by edge-space cooperative evolution and implicit-Euler limits. If a column fails, a one-edge quadratic and a single-step input give explicit strict amplification; the four-site example gives 5/6>1/2. The packaged Fraction checker verifies 126 exact inverse tests, 504 nonlinear quartic instances and the exact witness. Finite checks are not treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The nearest published tree-heat theorem covers the identical path edge-weight criterion for linear heat, but expressly does not establish nonlinear TV flow; the new claim concerns simultaneous sharp contractivity for every separable convex nonlinear proximal map and subgradient flow. Barbero--Sra and Kolmogorov--Pock--Rolinek provide algorithms for related minimization models, not the necessary-and-sufficient two-input weighted-BV contractivity statement. Targeted actual published-finding corpus and literature searches found no stronger covering statement; possible earlier equivalent nonlinear comparison results remain a residual risk.
residual_risks: An earlier equivalently formulated one-dimensional nonlinear diffusion comparison result may have escaped searches; no exhaustive historical priority claim is made.
The result is specific to separable convex edge interactions on finite paths, so it cannot be read as a tree or cyclic graph theorem.

value.rationale: A complete necessary-and-sufficient, conductance-independent and nonlinear-uniform stability classification for natural weighted BV perturbation metrics in 1D denoising and convex edge diffusion. It covers arbitrary finite convex interaction laws, including asymmetric smooth laws and nonsmooth TV penalties, while a concrete one-edge quadratic demonstrates exact failure outside the class. Nonconstant weights can qualify, and the criterion is a transparent superharmonic inequality. The motivation is stronger than a reparameterized matrix-norm computation: it characterizes all weighted variation metrics that remain stable simultaneously for an entire family of nonlinear operators and flows.
